To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for ideal and uniform weighting, the covariance of the fiducial registration errors is equal to the covariance of the target registration error, and that in the exact case, there is a one-to-one relationship between the two covariances, but that there is no measure of goodness of fit that gives any information about the variance of the target registration errors.

(1) for ideal weighting, fluctuations of FRE are independent of those of TRE; and (2) for ideal and uniform weighting, there are no useful measures that give to first-order information about the fluctuating nature of TRE.

the correlation of FRE and TRE in the exact case can be neglected for uniform weighting, that it is not negligible for ideal weighting, that it can be neglected for ideal weighting if the fiducials are randomly positioned and the FLE is randomly distributed, and that it is negligible for uniform weighting in all cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the statistical analysis of the errors associated with the registration of images of anatomical structures, which are used to guide surgical procedures, and with the design of registration algorithms that minimize the errors.
the analysis of the error in the registration of two sets of fiducial points, the first set of which are known and the second of which are to be determined.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the covariance of FRE, while it is related to the covariance of the TRE, should not be interpreted as a measure of TRE.
the only reliable measure of the accuracy of rigid registration is the variance of TRE.
for the weighting schemes employed in commercial surgical navigation systems, the covariance of FRE is not a good estimator of the variance of the TRE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
while it is important to have accurate fiducial localization, it is not possible to determine a priori the effect on registration accuracy of any particular localization error.
the covariance of FRE is a valid measure of registration accuracy only when the covariance of TRE is not a valid measure of the accuracy of registration, and vice versa.

, for ideal weighting, the first-order analysis is exact for the exact case, and for both ideal and for uniform weighting the first-order analysis provides a valid approximation of the first-order covariance of the TRE in the exact case.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the first-order analysis is a valuable tool in the development of guidance systems, as it provides the means to determine the effect of FLE on TRE, and thus the expected accuracy of registration, for arbitrary weightings and anistropy.

for the ideal and uniform weighting schemes, the variance of TRE is equal to the variance of the weighted FRE, and therefore the variance of FRE may be used as a surrogate measure of the variance of TRE.

, while it is possible to predict the covariance of the TRE from the covariance of FLE, there is no simple measure of goodness of fit for a given fiducial configuration, nor is there any simple measure of goodness that is independent of the covariance of FEL.
